AUTHOR: cph-prov-003
TEXT: Spontaneous vaginal birth at 39+4 weeks to a 31-year-old, para 1. Fetal movements were normal throughout and there were no maternal comorbidities. Growth scans and umbilical artery dopplers were both reported normal. As a low-risk labour no continuous CTG was used; liquor was clear with no meconium, no chorioamnionitis, membranes were ruptured well under 18 hours, and there were no red flags for sepsis. No sentinel event occurred. Birth weight 3420 g with Apgars 8 at one minute and 9 at five minutes (a ten-minute score was not required). Cord clamping was delayed for about 90 seconds. Paired cord gases were reassuring - arterial pH 7.28, base excess -3.4, lactate 3.1 - so no repeat sample was taken. The baby needed no intubation, no chest compressions and no drugs and went to the postnatal ward with mother. No hypoglycaemia and no neonatal unit admission; home on day 2. The unit-level audit questionnaire has been completed and local guidelines for cord-gas sampling and for fetal acidosis are both in place.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-003
TEXT: Born at 40+1 by emergency caesarean to a 37-year-old, para 2, whose pregnancy was complicated by gestational diabetes. Mother reported reduced fetal movements on admission. Scans and dopplers had both been normal antenatally and a CTG was running, which became pathological; the liquor was meconium-stained. There was no chorioamnionitis and membranes were under 18 hours, but the baby met red-flag sepsis criteria. No named sentinel event. Birth weight 3650 g; Apgars were low at 2, 5 and 7 across one, five and ten minutes. Cord clamping was not delayed. The arterial cord gas showed a severe metabolic acidosis - pH 7.03, base excess -15.2, lactate 10.6. The baby was intubated at delivery with chest compressions and a single dose of adrenaline, then admitted to the neonatal unit. A repeat gas at 2.0 hours showed lactate falling to 3.8 and the gas had fully normalised by 6.5 hours. No hypoglycaemia recorded. Discharged home on day 6. Unit audit questionnaire complete; cord-gas-sampling and fetal-acidosis guidelines both available locally.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-003
TEXT: First baby (para 0) delivered by forceps at 38+6 weeks; mother aged 27 with no comorbidities and normal movements. Antenatal scans and dopplers were both normal and a CTG was performed. Liquor was clear, there was no chorioamnionitis and no sepsis red flags, but membranes had been ruptured for more than 18 hours (PROM). No sentinel event. Birth weight 3180 g with Apgars 7 and 9 at one and five minutes; ten-minute score not required. Cord clamping was delayed. The arterial cord sample clotted, so no valid pH, base excess or lactate are available - this is flagged as a data-quality gap. The baby was vigorous, needed no resuscitation (no intubation, compressions or drugs) and stayed with mother on the postnatal ward. No repeat gas, no hypoglycaemia, no neonatal admission; home on day 2. Unit questionnaire completed and both local guidelines (cord-gas sampling and fetal acidosis) are available.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-003
TEXT: Emergency caesarean at 37+2 weeks for a placental abruption - the documented sentinel event - in a 39-year-old, para 3, with chronic hypertension and reduced fetal movements. Antenatal scans and dopplers were both abnormal (neither normal) and a CTG was in progress. Liquor was clear, no chorioamnionitis, membranes under 18 hours, but the baby met red-flag sepsis criteria. Birth weight 2910 g; Apgars were very low at 1, 3 and 5. Cord clamping was not delayed. The cord gas showed a profound acidosis - pH 6.91, base excess -21.4, lactate 14.2. The baby was intubated, received chest compressions and two doses of adrenaline, and was admitted to the neonatal unit. A repeat gas at 1.2 hours had lactate 8.9 and the gas normalised only by 18.0 hours. Hypoglycaemia was present. Discharged home on day 14. Unit-level questionnaire complete; both local guidelines in place.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-001
TEXT: Spontaneous vaginal birth at 41+0 weeks to a 34-year-old, para 1, with no comorbidities and normal fetal movements. Scans and dopplers normal antenatally; CTG performed. Liquor clear, no chorioamnionitis, membranes under 18 hours, no sepsis red flags. The delivery was complicated by a shoulder dystocia (recorded as the sentinel event), resolved within about 90 seconds. Large baby at 4120 g with Apgars 4, 8 and 9. Cord clamping not delayed. Cord gas pH 7.12, base excess -9.8, lactate 7.2. The baby needed stimulation and brief mask ventilation only - no intubation, no compressions, no drugs - and was nursed on transitional care. A repeat gas was sent and showed lactate 5.9, but the age at that repeat sample was never entered in the maternity record (data-quality gap) and the time to full normalisation is therefore not known. No hypoglycaemia. Home on day 3. Unit questionnaire completed; cord-gas and fetal-acidosis guidelines both available.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-005
TEXT: Preterm emergency caesarean at 35+5 weeks in a 41-year-old, para 4, with gestational diabetes and intrapartum pyrexia; the free-text comorbidity note records suspected intra-amniotic infection. Fetal movements normal. Scans and dopplers normal; CTG performed. Liquor clear with no meconium, but chorioamnionitis was present, membranes had been ruptured over 18 hours and the baby met sepsis red-flag criteria. No discrete sentinel event. Birth weight 2680 g; Apgars 5, 7 and 8. Cord clamping not delayed. Cord gas mildly acidotic - pH 7.18, base excess -8.1, lactate 6.4. The baby needed no intubation, compressions or drugs but was admitted to the neonatal unit for CPAP and antibiotics. Repeat gas at 3.0 hours showed lactate 4.8 and the gas had normalised by 4.5 hours. Hypoglycaemia was present. Discharged on day 8. Unit-level questionnaire complete and both local guidelines available.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-003
TEXT: Vacuum delivery for fetal distress at 39+0 weeks; mother 29, para 0 (first baby), no comorbidities. She had reported reduced movements before admission but the fetal-movements field in the electronic template was left as unknown, so that item cannot be confirmed. Growth scans were normal; the doppler result was not recorded (unknown). CTG performed. Liquor clear, no chorioamnionitis, membranes under 18 hours, but red-flag sepsis criteria were met. No sentinel event. Birth weight 3030 g with Apgars 6 and 9; ten-minute score not required. Cord clamping was not delayed. The arterial cord gas was reassuring with pH 7.24 and base excess -5.6; lactate was not measured on that sample. No resuscitation needed beyond the instrumental delivery (no intubation, compressions or drugs). Postnatal ward, no repeat gas, no hypoglycaemia, no neonatal admission; home on day 2. Unit questionnaire complete; both guidelines available.

TEXT: Uncomplicated water birth - spontaneous vaginal delivery at 40+3 weeks to a 36-year-old, para 2, no comorbidities, normal movements. Scans and dopplers both normal. No CTG was recorded because the low-risk intermittent-auscultation pathway was used. Liquor clear, no chorioamnionitis, membranes under 18 hours, no sepsis red flags. No sentinel event. Birth weight 3520 g with excellent Apgars of 9 and 10; ten-minute not required. Cord clamping delayed. Cord gases were normal - pH 7.31, base excess -2.2, lactate 2.4. No intubation, compressions or drugs. Stayed on the postnatal ward, no repeat gas, no hypoglycaemia, no neonatal admission; home on day 2. Unit-level audit questionnaire completed; local cord-gas-sampling and fetal-acidosis guidelines both in place.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-003
TEXT: Emergency caesarean at 38+1 weeks for a uterine rupture (the sentinel event) in a 38-year-old, para 2, with a previous caesarean and reduced fetal movements. Scans and dopplers normal; CTG performed. Liquor clear, no chorioamnionitis, membranes under 18 hours, but red-flag sepsis criteria met. Birth weight 3260 g; Apgars very low at 1, 4 and 6. Cord clamping not delayed. Severe acidosis on the cord gas - pH 6.98, base excess -18.7, lactate 12.8. The baby was intubated with chest compressions and one dose of adrenaline and admitted to the neonatal unit. Repeat gas at 1.5 hours showed lactate 7.2 and normalised by 12.0 hours. No hypoglycaemia. The age at discharge home was not captured in the maternity record (data-quality gap), and note that the CFM source is recorded inconsistently between teams. Unit questionnaire complete; both local guidelines available.

TEXT: Term spontaneous vaginal birth at 39+6 weeks to a 28-year-old, para 0 (first baby), whose only comorbidity is asthma; fetal movements normal. Liquor clear, no chorioamnionitis, membranes under 18 hours, no sepsis red flags. No sentinel event. Birth weight 3340 g with Apgars 8 and 9; ten-minute not required. Cord clamping delayed. Unit-level questionnaire completed and both local guidelines in place.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-004
TEXT: Admitted to the neonatal unit at 0.5 hours of age following emergency caesarean for a pathological CTG and meconium with a metabolic acidosis. Therapeutic cooling was started at 1.3 hours of age. The baby was not transferred out to another unit. CFM showed an abnormal background trace; there were no seizures - neither clinical nor electrographic - and no acute injury was seen on MRI. Total stay on the neonatal unit was 6 days and the baby went home on day 6, feeding from a bottle, with no abnormal neurology documented at discharge.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-004
TEXT: Neonatal unit admission at 0.4 hours of age after a placental abruption with severe acidosis. Cooling commenced at 1.1 hours. Not transferred out. The CFM was severely abnormal; seizures were present and were both clinically evident and confirmed electrographically. MRI demonstrated basal ganglia injury. The baby stayed 14 days in the unit and was discharged home on day 14 on combined tube and bottle feeds, with abnormal neurology still present at discharge.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-005
TEXT: Admitted at 0.8 hours of age with suspected sepsis on a background of maternal fever and chorioamnionitis, for CPAP and antibiotics. The baby was not cooled and CFM monitoring was not done. There were no seizures of any kind and MRI showed no injury. Not transferred out. Length of stay was 8 days with discharge home on day 8, breastfeeding, and no abnormal neurology at discharge.

AUTHOR: cph-prov-004
TEXT: Neonatal unit admission at 0.75 hours of age after uterine rupture and severe acidosis; cooling was started at 1.6 hours and the baby was later transferred out to a cooling centre. The CFM is documented inconsistently - the bedside note calls it normal while the formal neurology report records an abnormal trace with electrographic seizures; there were no clinically apparent seizures. MRI showed basal ganglia and thalamic injury. The baby spent 9 days on the unit. The age at discharge home was not recorded (data-quality gap). At the point of this note the baby was on tube feeds with abnormal neurology present.
